title: In 1848, Niagara Falls Stopped Flowing for 30 Hours

scenes.text: In 1848, Niagara Falls stopped flowing for thirty hours.
People woke up to a silent, dried-up river.
Some walked and rode horses across the exposed rock floor of the channel.
Strong winds had pushed ice from Lake Erie into the Niagara River.
The ice piled into a dam and cut off the water going over the falls.
Then the winds shifted, the ice broke, and the water came roaring back.

description:
On March 29, 1848, ice from Lake Erie jammed the Niagara River and the falls ran dry for about 30 hours.
People walked on the exposed riverbed.
Would you have walked out there?
first_comment: Would you have walked out onto the dry riverbed?
